analysis: What changed vs the 4am brief: (1) CoreWeave got worse overnight, not better - premarket -3.6% to -4.4% (~$66.61, Barron's/Reuters) vs -2.5% at 4am, and the freshest signal is the Reuters credit piece (1h ago): 9fin's Max Frumes calls it a 'turning point in the pricing and availability and structure of credit that's supporting the AI boom,' and F/m Investments' John Han says his desk is 'definitely taking another look' at AI-infrastructure exposure. The June bonds (9.675% at issue) now yield ~15%. This is the dominant risk signal, and it is credit-led, not equity-led. (2) Tesla is holding the Roadster pop - +4.4 to +4.8% premarket around $379.65, but HSBC's first take (Friday morning) framed it as 'an engineering flex rather than a demonstration of earnings power,' and the Barclays SpaceX-merger chatter remains pure speculation with no company confirmation - treat as fragile. (3) Two fresh single-name moves outside the core universe: Netflix -2.4% after replacing CCO Bela Bajaria with Peter Rice (effective Oct 26), coming a day after 6%/1,000 layoffs and with Q3 earnings Oct 20; Strategy -3% after MSCI approved rules that could exclude BTC-heavy companies from global indexes from Nov 30. (4) Futures firmed slightly since 4am - S&P +0.2%, Dow +0.3% - but Nasdaq 100 is still red (-0.2% per Reuters/Barron's; quotes disagree) and the 10Y has crept back above 5.11%, +4bps from Thursday. Signal: AI-credit repricing broadening (neoclouds + Oracle CDS records, chip pressure: MU -1.7%, AVGO -0.4% premarket); noise: the merger chatter and Roadster $80B market-cap math. Today's 8:30/9:15 ET data (import prices, industrial production) land with no Fed cushion - blackout starts Saturday.

headlines.headline: Futures mixed-to-higher ~5am ET: S&P 500 +0.2%, Dow +0.3% (+176 pts), Nasdaq 100 -0.2% (Reuters/Barron's live, <1h); Russell 2000 futures +0.4%. VIX ~16.03 premarket; 10Y back above 5.11%, +~4bps from Thursday's close (Investopedia, <1h). After Warsh's IMF remarks, CME odds of an October hike sit at 15% (85% hold), December hike at 89%. Week-to-date: Nasdaq -2.4% (four-week win streak ending), S&P -0.9%, Dow +1%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A firmer but still split tape - the defensive rotation is holding but Nasdaq red and 10Y creeping back up mean rate-and-credit anxiety is not cleared; the 8:30/9:15 ET data hits with no Fed cover.

headlines.headline: Tesla +4.4% to +4.8% in premarket trade (~$379.65, Barron's <1h) after Thursday's Roadster reveal; SpaceX +2.1% (Reuters, <1h). HSBC's Friday first take: 'an engineering flex rather than a demonstration of earnings power; still some wait for first deliveries' (production targeted 2028). Barron's: the move added ~$80B in market value - roughly Ferrari's whole market cap. Barclays' Dan Levy's SpaceX-merger-before-Dec-6 speculation resurfaced (single-source, no company confirmation).
headlines.why_it_matters: Sentiment-driven halo holding into the morning, but HSBC's 'engineering flex' framing and the speculative merger chatter mean the pop is priced on spectacle - single-source rumor, treat as fragile; Oct 21 earnings are the real test.

headlines.headline: CoreWeave -3.6% to -4.4% premarket (~$66.61, Barron's/Reuters <1h), falling for the sixth time in seven sessions and down ~15% over five trading days, as the bond rout takes center stage: its June-issued 9.675% notes now yield ~15% (Reuters, 1h). 9fin's Max Frumes: a 'turning point in the pricing and availability and structure of credit that's supporting the AI boom'; F/m Investments' John Han says the desk is 'definitely taking another look' at AI-infrastructure exposure. BNP Paribas' Daniel Wang ($169 target) warns traditional debt financing is 'increasingly uneconomic' without improving credit confidence.
headlines.why_it_matters: Credit is now the price-action driver, not equity - the Frumes 'turning point' quote says bond desks are repricing all AI-linked debt, and Huang's defense stopped working overnight; that is the tape's central risk signal.

headlines.headline: Chips still under pressure in premarket: Nebius -2%, Iren -2%, Micron -1.7%, Broadcom -0.4% (Reuters, <1h). The SOX fell for its seventh straight day Thursday (-0.88%) despite TSMC's 68.7% profit jump. CDS spreads for big tech hit record highs this week (LSEG/S&P Global MI via reporting): CoreWeave, Oracle at records; Amazon, Alphabet, Meta also at records, albeit slower-widening.
headlines.why_it_matters: The stress is spreading from neocloud balance sheets up the stack - record CDS across big tech says the market is pricing financing risk into the whole AI capex chain, not just CoreWeave.

headlines.headline: Megacap roundup (Thursday closes, carried): AAPL -0.28% after its first-ever $5T close; MSFT +1.08%, GOOGL +0.45%, AMZN +0.27%, META -0.11%. Meta launched Muse Spark Open, an 816B MoE coding model (single-source, unverified by major outlets). Tesla Q3 earnings land Oct 21 - the first Magnificent Seven print this season.
headlines.why_it_matters: The capex-restraint premium (Apple) vs. spender discount (AI builders) remains the megacap positioning frame; Tesla's Oct 21 print is the first real test of whether spectacle converts to numbers.

headlines.headline: Netflix -2.4% premarket (Barron's <1h) after naming former Disney/Fox exec Peter Rice as chief content officer, succeeding Bela Bajaria effective Oct 26 (Reuters, Thursday). The shakeup follows a 6%/~1,000-person layoff - its biggest since 2022; WSJ: stock down nearly 40% over the past year and engagement growth is stalling. Q3 earnings report Oct 20.
headlines.why_it_matters: A leadership reset at a content giant trading at a deep 1-year loss - markets read the CCO change as confirmation the engagement-growth problem is real, and Oct 20 earnings is five days out.

headlines.headline: Strategy (MSTR) -3% premarket after MSCI approved new rules that could exclude companies holding mainly nonoperating assets - including Bitcoin treasuries - from its global equity indexes from Nov 30 (Barron's <1h).
headlines.why_it_matters: Index-inclusion risk is now a mechanical overhang on the BTC-treasury trade - forced-selling flows matter more to holders than the coin's price on this read.

headlines.headline: Friday macro (all ET): import/export price indices at 8:30 (consensus: imports +0.6% to +0.8% m/m, exports +0.9% - CME/WSJ surveys), industrial production and capacity utilization at 9:15 (consensus: IP +0.4% m/m after flat August, capacity 76.5% vs 76.3%). Last day of Fed speak before Saturday's blackout ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC.
headlines.why_it_matters: Post-hot-CPI/PPI, trade-price inflation feeds straight into the December-hike-odds calculus - and with the blackout starting Saturday, there is no Fed speaker to walk back a hot print.
